I'm a website developer, so I have some input for UI/UX. Here are my most important things for a potential Voat app, in order:

*Readability - everything else means nothing if it's hard to read. Use sans-serif fonts, decent line spacing / kerning, and readable font sizes.

*Extremely easy navigation - Your cool features are useless if people can't find them. Put a lot of energy into layout and navigation

*Good use of whitespace - Think like the page of a book. Have decent margins and padding so things don't look cluttered

*No crazy colors - keep tones muted, neutral, and easy to look at

*Light / Dark theme - Many of us enjoy looking at a dark screen with light text instead of the standard reverse

*NO ADS - For the love of all that is good, no ads, even in the free version. Sell the paid version with cool extra features, but don't make the free users look at ads. We don't click them anyway, we just close them. They break UX pretty hard.

BaconReader is a pretty great example of how this can be done right. However, there are still tons of improvements that could be made. I will update this comment as I think of more.

Philosophy

Don't know, to be honest.

What should it look like?

This is one of those "I'd let the user decide" things. Personally, I'm a fan of curved edges, much like Chrome's tabs. Other people like hard corners and lines, like those found in Vivaldi or the Windows Metro interface. I'm also a fan of dark themes, using one system-wide, while others prefer a bright theme.

I do think one thing should be kept in mind: It should be made to not look cluttered. IIRC, Reddit Is Fun did a decent job of that with its swipe functionality: If you want to view the content on a post, tap it. If you want to access anything more, swipe it to the side to reveal a short, but full, menu of what you could do on the main site. Looks nice, isn't cluttered, and works fine.
